presentingComplaint: Progressive drowsiness, constipation and polyuria over 10 days on a background of known metastatic breast cancer
history: Ten-day history of increasing lethargy, generalised weakness, anorexia, nausea, marked thirst and polyuria, and worsening constipation. Family report intermittent confusion for the past 48 hours. Known ER-positive invasive ductal breast carcinoma diagnosed 3 years ago, now with radiologically confirmed bone metastases; on an aromatase inhibitor. No fever, cough, dysuria or diarrhoea. Not on thiazides, lithium, calcium or vitamin D supplements. No prior renal disease.
examination: Drowsy but rousable, dry mucous membranes and reduced skin turgor consistent with volume depletion. Abdomen soft with sluggish bowel sounds; no peritonism. No focal neurological deficit, no neck stiffness, no papilloedema. No cellulitis, calf tenderness or focal source of infection. Chest clear.
imaging: Known lytic bony metastases on prior CT/bone scan; no new acute findings. CT head (done for confusion) unremarkable.
differentialDiagnoses: Dehydration / acute kidney injury from another cause
citations: Harrison 22e — Disorders of the Parathyroid Gland and Calcium Homeostasis / Hypercalcemia
ASCO Management of Hypercalcemia of Malignancy 2023
contraindications: Loop diuretics only after adequate volume repletion, not for routine calcium lowering
Bisphosphonate dosing must be adjusted for renal impairment; ensure adequate hydration before zoledronate
Avoid nephrotoxins and further volume depletion given creatinine 1.6 mg/dL
edgeCases: Concurrent primary hyperparathyroidism can coexist with malignancy — an inappropriately non-suppressed PTH should prompt reassessment
Calcium >3.5 mmol/L with obtundation is a hypercalcaemic crisis requiring urgent aggressive therapy
Denosumab is the preferred bone-targeted agent in significant renal impairment where bisphosphonates are contraindicated
expectedMaiK: Suppressed PTH with elevated PTHrP and lytic bone disease in a patient with known metastatic breast cancer confirms hypercalcaemia of malignancy; initiate aggressive isotonic saline rehydration and a bone-resorption inhibitor (IV bisphosphonate or denosumab), and treat the underlying tumour.
expectedNextQuestions: What is the albumin-corrected calcium and the PTH level?
Is the patient on thiazides, lithium, calcium or vitamin D supplements?
What is the level of consciousness and urine output?
regressionAssertions: differential must not include any infective diagnosis
